comments.text_zh: 得益于代数数据类型（Algebraic Data Types），这套类型系统比 Java/C#/C++ 中的类型系统表达能力强得多。Yaron Minsky（Jane Street，OCaml 最大用户）创造了“让非法状态无法表示”这个说法，用来解释 ADT 如何帮助我们争取到编译器的协助，从而正确表达我们的意图；而 Richard Feldman（NoRedInk，Elm 最大用户）做过一场堪称瑰宝的演讲，用贴近生活、具体实在的例子深入探讨了这个理念。演讲题目是“Making Impossible States Impossible”，应该能很好地阐明这个概念。[VIDEO]
comments.text: The type system is a lot more expressive than the ones found in Java/C#/C++, thanks to Algebraic Data Types. Yaron Minsky (Jane Street, largest OCaml user) coined the term "make invalid states unrepresentable" to explain how ADTs help in enlisting the help of the compiler to help us express our intent correctly, and Richard Feldman (NoRedInk, largest Elm user) has given an absolute gem of a talk that dives into that idea with relatable, concrete examples. It is titled "Making Impossible States Impossible" and should clarify this concept nicely. [VIDEO]

comments.author: jasim
comments.story_title: Writing ReasonML Bindings for JavaScript APIs
comments.text_zh: 映射是逃不掉的。无论用的是 Reason、PureScript、Elm 还是 Fable——如果你想享受类型带来的好处，就必须把传入的数据解析成静态类型。好消息是，你可以基于对数据形状和结构的可靠保证来构建系统的其余部分。不用做 null 检查，不用担心缺失的键。如果你在解析时足够小心，那么当传入数据格式不正确（缺少键，甚至有多余的键）时，就可以抛出异常或返回 None。Reason/BuckleScript 跑在 Javascript 运行时上时，也有一个 `Js.t` 类型，基本上就是 Javascript 对象。你确实需要定义它的形状，类似于定义 record 类型，但不需要把它转换成原生 record。JS 数组也得到原生支持——它和 BuckleScript 的 array 一一对应。我喜欢把数组转换成列表，因为它们更适合基于值的编程（在递归函数里对 [head, ...tail] 做模式匹配）。而且，如果你以让无效状态不可能出现的方式来创建类型，你就把系统后续整个生命周期内开展工作所需的认知负担降低了一个数量级。以下是一些关于这项出色编程技术的资源： - [LINK] - [VIDEO] - [LINK] - [LINK]
comments.text: There is no escaping the mapping. It doesn't matter if it is Reason or PureScript, Elm, or Fable - you have to parse the incoming data into a static type if you want to enjoy the benefits of types. The good thing is that you can build the rest of your system with a firm guarantee on the shape and structure of the data. No null checks, no missing keys. If you are careful with your parsing you can raise exceptions or return None if the incoming data is not well-formed (missing keys or even extra keys). Reason/BuckleScript when run on a Javascript runtime also has a `Js.t` type which is basically the Javascript object. You do have to define the shape of it similar to how you'd define a record type, but you don't need to convert it into a native record. JS arrays are also natively supported - it maps 1:1 to BuckleScript's array. I like to convert arrays into lists since they are better suited for value-based programming (pattern-matching over [head, ...tail] inside recursive functions). And if you create your types in a way that invalid states are impossible, you've just reduced the cognitive load needed to work on the system for the rest of its life by an order of magnitude. Here are some resources on this wonderful programming technique: - [LINK] - [VIDEO] - [LINK] - [LINK]

comments.author: jasim
comments.story_title: Ask HN: How to improve code quality while maintaining decent velocity?
comments.quote_zh: 学会先考虑类型，而把算法看作数据结构自然产生的结果。
comments.text_zh: * 学会先考虑类型，而把算法看作数据结构自然产生的结果。Richard Feldman：[VIDEO]；* 使用支持快速重构的静态类型语言。理想情况下是带类型的函数式语言，比如 Elm、Reason、OCaml 或 Haskell。我最近交付了一个复杂的 JavaScript 项目（没有类型），这是我从业十年来少数几次对自己写的代码健壮性有如此信心的情况之一。即使出现意外情况，它在生产环境中依然稳固。这要归功于我培养的类型化函数式编程习惯：在系统边界处解析并验证所有数据；通过数据建模让不一致的状态无法出现，从而实现更好的设计；并始终自动处理所有边界情况。所以，即使你在工作场所并不实际使用这类语言，学习它确实有回报，能让你整体上成为更好的程序员。
comments.text: * Learn to think about types first, and the algorithms as a natural consequence of the structure of your data. Richard Feldman: [VIDEO] , * Use a statically typed language that allows fast refactoring. Ideally a typed functional language like Elm, Reason, OCaml, or Haskell. I recently shipped a complex Javascript project (without types) and it is one of the few instances of my decade-old professional career where I had that level of confidence in the robustness of a piece of code I wrote. It remained sturdy in production even in the presence of unforeseen conditions. This was thanks to the habits I picked up from typed FP: parsing and validating all data at the boundaries of the system, better design by modelling data to make inconsistent states impossible, and automatically handling all edge-cases at all times. So even if you don't actively use such a language in your workplace, there really is a payoff to learning it in making you a better programmer overall.

comments.author: jon49
comments.text_zh: 像 F# 这样的语言在静态类型和动态类型之间提供了一个很好的平衡点。它有 Type Providers，可以在你输入代码时动态地“生成”代码。你不需要指定所有类型，它会为你推断出很多类型。所以几乎感觉像是在写动态语言，但它会告诉你是否写错了。除非一门语言有 Type Providers，否则我不会认为它是现代的；我认为这是一个非常关键的特性。我相信 Idris 和 F# 是仅有的具备这一特性的语言。人们正在推动 TypeScript 加入这一特性——谁知道会不会实现呢。很多人说，如果你用的是动态语言，只需要保持自律并写大量测试。而使用像 F# 这样优秀的静态类型语言，你甚至无法为某些业务逻辑编写测试，因为你写代码的方式让“impossible states impossible”，见 [VIDEO]
comments.text: Languages like F# give a nice sweet spot between static typing and dynamic typing. It has Type Providers that "generate" code on the fly as you are typing. You don't need to specify all the types, it will infer many types for you. So, you almost feel like you are writing in a dynamic language but you it tells you if you are writing something incorrectly. I would not consider a language to be modern unless it has Type Providers I consider this to be such an essential feature. I believe Idris and F# are the only languages that have it. People are trying to push TypeScript to add it - who knows if it will happen. Many are saying that if you have a dynamic language you just need to be disciplined and write many tests. With good static typed languages like F# you can't even write tests on certain business logic since the way you write your code you make "impossible states impossible", see [VIDEO]

comments.author: jasim
comments.text_zh: ReasonML 在我看来已经相当适合生产工作，如果你用它配合 NodeJS 构建服务端应用，或用 React（ReasonReact）构建富前端应用。Reason 的目标受众（至少目前）是那些想提升程序员水平、想构建优雅而稳固的生产系统的 Web 应用开发者。Reason 和 Elm 一起正在让静态类型函数式编程民主化，我相信未来 10 年编程语言版图会发生巨大变化，类型化 FP 的实践终将进入主流商业编程。Reason 的吸引力在于它把 OCaml 打包到 Web 浏览器（这由 BuckleScript 实现——真正做重活的 OCaml 到 JS 编译器），它的语法对当今绝大多数程序员来说很熟悉，以及团队发布的大量绑定、库和文档生态。OCaml 是一门非常务实的语言；它的主要吸引力在于强大的静态类型系统和不可变、函数式编程，但 OCaml 里的“O”代表“Objective”——它是 CAML 的一个实现，支持面向对象编程。但你几乎从不需要对象。OCaml 的模块系统及其惯用法让你无需可变状态就能写出封装良好的代码，而当你确实需要写贴近底层的命令式代码时，你可以尽情去写，因为 OCaml 不像 Has 那样是“纯”函数式语言
comments.text: ReasonML is IMO quite ready for production work if you use it for building server-side applications with NodeJS or rich front-end applications with React (ReasonReact). The target audience for Reason (at least for the moment) are web application developers who want to level up as programmers and want to build elegant, sturdy production systems. Reason and Elm together are democratizing statically typed functional programming and I believe that the next 10 years are going to see a massive change in the programming language landscape, with the practice of typed FP finally finding adoption in mainstream commercial programming. The allure of Reason is in its packaging of OCaml to the web browser (which is made possible by BuckleScript - the actual OCaml to JS compiler doing the heavy lifting), its syntax that is familiar to the vast majority of programmers today, and the large ecosystem of bindings, libraries, and documentation that the team has put out. OCaml is a very pragmatic language; its main pull is its powerful static type system and immutable, functional programming, but the "O" in OCaml stands for "Objective" - it is an implementation of CAML with support for object-oriented programming. But you almost never need objects. OCaml's module system and its idioms allows you to write well-encapsulated code without mutation, and when you actually need to write honest to metal imperative code, you can do it with abandon because OCaml is not a "pure" functional language like Has

comments.author: nateabele
comments.story_title: We use TypeScript not based on preference, but because we want to make money
comments.why_zh: 引用来说明类型如何消除无法测试的无效状态
comments.text_zh: 当然，但重点是，一个还算像样的类型系统能消除整类错误——从而消除你本来需要为之写测试的一大片东西。更重要的是，一个好的类型系统会帮你做到“Make Impossible States Impossible”[0]——甚至更多行为你都不必测试，因为坏行为根本无法在你的程序里表示出来。在局部，测试的威力严格更强，因为测试可以任意复杂；但我会说，一个（真正好的）类型系统在整体上更强，因为就整体程序正确性而言，你能获得大得多的杠杆。我很多个人项目是用 Elm 写的（对对对，尽管来喷）——模型定义得非常好，但测试套件通常只有少数几个测试，针对我真正想验证的行为。我甚至还没玩过 property checker，但话说回来，这东西严格比单元测试更强，可你只有拥有类型系统才能得到它*。[0] [VIDEO] * 好吧，这并不完全正确：看看 Clojure 里的 clojure.spec——但反例太少了，所以就大多数实际用途而言，这是成立的
comments.text: Sure, but the point is, a halfway decent type system will eliminate whole classes of errors—consequently eliminating whole swaths of things you would ever need to write tests for. What's more, though, is that a good type system will help you 'Make Impossible States Impossible'[0]—even more behavior you don't have to test because bad behavior is simply not representable in your program. Tests are strictly more powerful in the small, because they can be arbitrarily complex, but I would say a (really good) type system is more powerful in the large, because you get way more leverage in terms of overall program correctness. A lot of my personal projects are in Elm (yeah, yeah, bring on the hate)—the models are really well-defined, but the test suites usually only have a handful of tests of behavior I really want to verify. Haven't even played with the property checker yet, but again, that's something that is strictly more powerful than unit tests, but you can only get it* if you have a type system. [0] [VIDEO] * Okay that's not really true: see clojure.spec in Clojure—but there are so few counterexamples that it's true for most practical purposes
